Establish repository facts yourself before asking the user.\r\n\r\nFor behavior-changing work, invoke the `grilling` skill:\r\n\r\n- Start with a short clarification round for a straightforward change. Expand into a full design-tree interview when decisions are ambiguous, risky, or have competing solutions.\r\n- Ask all currently answerable questions in a round, number them, and give a recommended answer for each. Wait for the user's answers, then recompute the next question frontier.\r\n- Do not ask the user to discover facts available in the repository or environment.\r\n- When the frontier is settled, present a concise shared-understanding summary covering requirements, constraints, scenarios, design choices, and material test seams. Wait for explicit user confirmation before treating the specification as approved or implementing. If the user declines or asks to stop, stop.\r\n\r\n## 2. Specify and write BDD scenarios\r\n\r\nStore approved feature artifacts under `specs/<feature-name>/`. `.scratch/` may hold temporary discovery notes and issue-tracking tickets; promote the approved specification into `specs/` before implementation.\r\n\r\nFor a feature, enhancement, or significant change, create or update:\r\n\r\n- `spec.md`: requirements, constraints, acceptance criteria, and stable-ID Given/When/Then scenarios.\r\n- `design.md`: architecture, components, API contracts, data model, and material test seams.\r\n- `plan.md`: implementation approach and milestones.\r\n- `task.md`: ordered tasks and validation evidence.\r\n\r\nFor a narrow bug fix, use a concise `spec.md` for the expected behavior and relevant scenarios, plus `task.md` for implementation and test evidence. Add `design.md` or `plan.md` when the fix has material design or sequencing decisions. Expand the artifacts if the scope grows.\r\n\r\nTrace every acceptance criterion to one or more BDD scenarios. Include meaningful failure and boundary cases; do not create a separate scenario for every trivial variant. BDD scenarios describe observable behavior and are the source for implementation-level test coverage.\r\n\r\n## 3. Review before implementation\r\n\r\nConfirm that:\r\n\r\n- The user-approved understanding, requirements, and constraints are reflected in the spec.\r\n- Acceptance criteria and BDD scenarios are clear, observable, and traceable.\r\n- The design, public test seams, and test layers fit the architecture and have no unresolved material decisions.\r\n- Tasks are actionable and small enough for vertical implementation slices.\r\n\r\nResolve gaps with the user before implementation. Do not implement behavior outside the approved specification.\r\n\r\n## 4. Implement BDD-first with TDD\r\n\r\nUse BDD to define behavior, then TDD to implement it at the most appropriate test layer. Trace each scenario to automated verification, choosing the lowest practical layer that proves the behavior. Reserve end-to-end tests for journeys that need cross-boundary validation; a scenario does not require a one-to-one end-to-end test.\r\n\r\nWork in vertical slices, one behavior at a time:\r\n\r\n1. **Red:** Add a meaningful test for an approved behavior and run it. Confirm it fails because the behavior is missing or incorrect, not because of setup or environment failure.\r\n2. **Green:** Make the smallest production change that passes the test and relevant existing tests.\r\n3. **Refactor:** Improve the code while keeping the tests green.\r\n\r\nRecord the test layer, command, expected Red result, and Green result in `task.md`. If the Red test cannot be run, record the blocker and do not claim that the TDD cycle is complete. For non-behavioral edits, a new failing test is unnecessary; mechanical refactors still need characterization coverage for the behavior they preserve.\r\n\r\nFollow the applicable coding standards:\r\n\r\n- `docs/backend/coding.standard.md`\r\n- `docs/frontend/coding.standard.md`\r\n\r\n## 5. Verify and complete\r\n\r\n- Run relevant tests, lint, type-check, and build commands for the affected projects.\r\n- Verify each acceptance criterion against its BDD scenarios and test evidence.\r\n- Check for regressions and unintended behavior changes.\r\n- Keep the implementation, specification, design, plan, and task evidence synchronized.\r\n- Mark tasks complete only when their checks have actually run and passed.\r\n\r\nReport what changed, important decisions, actual validation results, and remaining limitations. Never claim a test or validation passed unless it was executed.\r\n---\r\nname: tdd\r\ndescription: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions \"red-green-refactor\", or wants integration tests.\r\n---\r\n\r\n# Test-Driven Development\r\n\r\nTDD is the red → green → refactor loop. For behavior-changing work, start from the user-approved BDD scenarios in the feature spec, then implement one vertical slice at a time. This skill is the reference that makes each cycle produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle: consult them before and during the loop, not after.\r\n\r\nWhen exploring the codebase, read `CONTEXT.md` (if it exists) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.\r\n\r\n## What a good test is\r\n\r\nTests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't. A good test reads like a specification: \"user can checkout with valid cart\" tells you exactly what capability exists, and it survives refactors because it doesn't care about internal structure.\r\n\r\nSee [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.\r\n\r\n## Seams: where tests go\r\n\r\nA **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.\r\n\r\n**Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam. You can't test everything, so agreeing the seams up front is how testing effort lands on the critical paths and complex logic instead of every edge case.\r\n\r\nAsk: \"What's the public interface, and which seams should we test?\"\r\n\r\nWhen the shape of that interface is itself in question (how deep the module is, where the seam belongs, what the interface should expose), call the Skill tool with \"codebase-design\" for the vocabulary. It is the shared source of the module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage and locality terms, and it is a reference to consult, not a session to run.\r\n\r\n## Anti-patterns\r\n\r\n- **Implementation-coupled**: mocks internal collaborators, tests private methods, or verifies through a side channel (querying the database instead of using the interface). The tell: the test breaks when you refactor but behavior hasn't changed.\r\n- **Tautological**: the assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does (`expect(add(a, b)).toBe(a + b)`, a snapshot derived by hand the same way, a constant asserted equal to itself), so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth: a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.\r\n- **Horizontal slicing**: writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead: one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.\r\n\r\n## Rules of the loop\r\n\r\n- **Red before green.** Write and run the failing test first. Confirm it fails because the approved behavior is missing or incorrect, then add only enough code to pass it. Don't anticipate future tests or add speculative features.\r\n- **One slice at a time.** Implement one behavior at one appropriate public seam per cycle. Trace the test to its BDD scenario; do not bulk-write tests before implementation.\r\n- **Refactor after green.** Improve the implementation while keeping the tests green. Independent code review remains a separate quality gate.\r\n- If a test cannot run, record the blocker and do not claim a completed TDD cycle.\r\n---\r\nname: grilling\r\ndescription: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.\r\n---\r\n\r\nInterview the user relentlessly until you reach a shared understanding. Map this as a **design tree**: every decision branches into the decisions that hang off it.\r\n\r\nWork the tree in **rounds**. The **frontier** is every decision whose prerequisites are already settled: the questions you can ask _now_ without guessing at answers you haven't heard yet. Ask the whole frontier in one round: number each question and give your recommended answer. Then wait for the user's answers before the next round.\r\n\r\nFormat a round like so:\r\n\r\n```\r\n❓ **Q1** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>\r\n\r\n➡️ <your recommended answer>\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n❓ **Q2** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>\r\n\r\n➡️ <your recommended answer>\r\n```\r\n\r\nEach round the user answers reshapes the tree: settled decisions push the frontier outward and unblock questions that depended on them. Recompute the frontier and ask the next round. A question whose answer depends on another question still open in this round belongs to a _later_ round, not this one.\r\n\r\nFinding _facts_ is your job, never the user's. When a frontier question needs a fact from the environment (filesystem, tools, etc.), dispatch a sub-agent to find it; don't ask the user for anything you could look up yourself. Don't block on it: a running exploration is an unsettled prerequisite, so only the questions downstream of it wait for the sub-agent to report; ask the rest of the frontier now. The _decisions_ are the user's: put each to them and wait.\r\n\r\nThe session is done when the frontier is empty: every branch of the design tree visited, nothing left silently assumed. Do not act on it until the user confirms you have reached a shared understanding.\r\n"}}

Scale the documentation to the change, but keep the clarification, BDD, and TDD gates for behavior changes.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 1. Understand and clarify\\r\\n\\r\\nInspect the existing implementation, related tests, architecture, project context, applicable coding standards, and available test commands. Establish repository facts yourself before asking the user.\\r\\n\\r\\nFor behavior-changing work, invoke the `grilling` skill:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Start with a short clarification round for a straightforward change. Expand into a full design-tree interview when decisions are ambiguous, risky, or have competing solutions.\\r\\n- Ask all currently answerable questions in a round, number them, and give a recommended answer for each. Wait for the user's answers, then recompute the next question frontier.\\r\\n- Do not ask the user to discover facts available in the repository or environment.\\r\\n- When the frontier is settled, present a concise shared-understanding summary covering requirements, constraints, scenarios, design choices, and material test seams. Wait for explicit user confirmation before treating the specification as approved or implementing. If the user declines or asks to stop, stop.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 2. Specify and write BDD scenarios\\r\\n\\r\\nStore approved feature artifacts under `specs/<feature-name>/`. `.scratch/` may hold temporary discovery notes and issue-tracking tickets; promote the approved specification into `specs/` before implementation.\\r\\n\\r\\nFor a feature, enhancement, or significant change, create or update:\\r\\n\\r\\n- `spec.md`: requirements, constraints, acceptance criteria, and stable-ID Given/When/Then scenarios.\\r\\n- `design.md`: architecture, components, API contracts, data model, and material test seams.\\r\\n- `plan.md`: implementation approach and milestones.\\r\\n- `task.md`: ordered tasks and validation evidence.\\r\\n\\r\\nFor a narrow bug fix, use a concise `spec.md` for the expected behavior and relevant scenarios, plus `task.md` for implementation and test evidence. Add `design.md` or `plan.md` when the fix has material design or sequencing decisions. Expand the artifacts if the scope grows.\\r\\n\\r\\nTrace every acceptance criterion to one or more BDD scenarios. Include meaningful failure and boundary cases; do not create a separate scenario for every trivial variant. BDD scenarios describe observable behavior and are the source for implementation-level test coverage.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 3. Review before implementation\\r\\n\\r\\nConfirm that:\\r\\n\\r\\n- The user-approved understanding, requirements, and constraints are reflected in the spec.\\r\\n- Acceptance criteria and BDD scenarios are clear, observable, and traceable.\\r\\n- The design, public test seams, and test layers fit the architecture and have no unresolved material decisions.\\r\\n- Tasks are actionable and small enough for vertical implementation slices.\\r\\n\\r\\nResolve gaps with the user before implementation. Do not implement behavior outside the approved specification.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 4. Implement BDD-first with TDD\\r\\n\\r\\nUse BDD to define behavior, then TDD to implement it at the most appropriate test layer. Trace each scenario to automated verification, choosing the lowest practical layer that proves the behavior. Reserve end-to-end tests for journeys that need cross-boundary validation; a scenario does not require a one-to-one end-to-end test.\\r\\n\\r\\nWork in vertical slices, one behavior at a time:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Red:** Add a meaningful test for an approved behavior and run it. Confirm it fails because the behavior is missing or incorrect, not because of setup or environment failure.\\r\\n2. **Green:** Make the smallest production change that passes the test and relevant existing tests.\\r\\n3. **Refactor:** Improve the code while keeping the tests green.\\r\\n\\r\\nRecord the test layer, command, expected Red result, and Green result in `task.md`. If the Red test cannot be run, record the blocker and do not claim that the TDD cycle is complete. For non-behavioral edits, a new failing test is unnecessary; mechanical refactors still need characterization coverage for the behavior they preserve.\\r\\n\\r\\nFollow the applicable coding standards:\\r\\n\\r\\n- `docs/backend/coding.standard.md`\\r\\n- `docs/frontend/coding.standard.md`\\r\\n\\r\\n## 5. Verify and complete\\r\\n\\r\\n- Run relevant tests, lint, type-check, and build commands for the affected projects.\\r\\n- Verify each acceptance criterion against its BDD scenarios and test evidence.\\r\\n- Check for regressions and unintended behavior changes.\\r\\n- Keep the implementation, specification, design, plan, and task evidence synchronized.\\r\\n- Mark tasks complete only when their checks have actually run and passed.\\r\\n\\r\\nReport what changed, important decisions, actual validation results, and remaining limitations. Never claim a test or validation passed unless it was executed.\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: tdd\\r\\ndescription: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions \\\"red-green-refactor\\\", or wants integration tests.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Test-Driven Development\\r\\n\\r\\nTDD is the red → green → refactor loop. For behavior-changing work, start from the user-approved BDD scenarios in the feature spec, then implement one vertical slice at a time. This skill is the reference that makes each cycle produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle: consult them before and during the loop, not after.\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen exploring the codebase, read `CONTEXT.md` (if it exists) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.\\r\\n\\r\\n## What a good test is\\r\\n\\r\\nTests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't. A good test reads like a specification: \\\"user can checkout with valid cart\\\" tells you exactly what capability exists, and it survives refactors because it doesn't care about internal structure.\\r\\n\\r\\nSee [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Seams: where tests go\\r\\n\\r\\nA **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam. You can't test everything, so agreeing the seams up front is how testing effort lands on the critical paths and complex logic instead of every edge case.\\r\\n\\r\\nAsk: \\\"What's the public interface, and which seams should we test?\\\"\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen the shape of that interface is itself in question (how deep the module is, where the seam belongs, what the interface should expose), call the Skill tool with \\\"codebase-design\\\" for the vocabulary. It is the shared source of the module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage and locality terms, and it is a reference to consult, not a session to run.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Anti-patterns\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Implementation-coupled**: mocks internal collaborators, tests private methods, or verifies through a side channel (querying the database instead of using the interface). The tell: the test breaks when you refactor but behavior hasn't changed.\\r\\n- **Tautological**: the assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does (`expect(add(a, b)).toBe(a + b)`, a snapshot derived by hand the same way, a constant asserted equal to itself), so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth: a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.\\r\\n- **Horizontal slicing**: writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead: one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Rules of the loop\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Red before green.** Write and run the failing test first. Confirm it fails because the approved behavior is missing or incorrect, then add only enough code to pass it. Don't anticipate future tests or add speculative features.\\r\\n- **One slice at a time.** Implement one behavior at one appropriate public seam per cycle. Trace the test to its BDD scenario; do not bulk-write tests before implementation.\\r\\n- **Refactor after green.** Improve the implementation while keeping the tests green. Independent code review remains a separate quality gate.\\r\\n- If a test cannot run, record the blocker and do not claim a completed TDD cycle.\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: grilling\\r\\ndescription: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nInterview the user relentlessly until you reach a shared understanding. Map this as a **design tree**: every decision branches into the decisions that hang off it.\\r\\n\\r\\nWork the tree in **rounds**. The **frontier** is every decision whose prerequisites are already settled: the questions you can ask _now_ without guessing at answers you haven't heard yet. Ask the whole frontier in one round: number each question and give your recommended answer. Then wait for the user's answers before the next round.\\r\\n\\r\\nFormat a round like so:\\r\\n\\r\\n```\\r\\n❓ **Q1** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>\\r\\n\\r\\n➡️ <your recommended answer>\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n❓ **Q2** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>\\r\\n\\r\\n➡️ <your recommended answer>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nEach round the user answers reshapes the tree: settled decisions push the frontier outward and unblock questions that depended on them. Recompute the frontier and ask the next round. A question whose answer depends on another question still open in this round belongs to a _later_ round, not this one.\\r\\n\\r\\nFinding _facts_ is your job, never the user's. When a frontier question needs a fact from the environment (filesystem, tools, etc.), dispatch a sub-agent to find it; don't ask the user for anything you could look up yourself. Don't block on it: a running exploration is an unsettled prerequisite, so only the questions downstream of it wait for the sub-agent to report; ask the rest of the frontier now. The _decisions_ are the user's: put each to them and wait.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe session is done when the frontier is empty: every branch of the design tree visited, nothing left silently assumed. Do not act on it until the user confirms you have reached a shared understanding.\\r\\n\"}}"

Good and Bad Tests\r\n\r\n## Good Tests\r\n\r\n**Integration-style**: Test through real interfaces, not mocks of internal parts.\r\n\r\n```typescript\r\n// GOOD: Tests observable behavior\r\ntest(\"user can checkout with valid cart\", async () => {\r\n  const cart = createCart();\r\n  cart.add(product);\r\n  const result = await checkout(cart, paymentMethod);\r\n  expect(result.status).toBe(\"confirmed\");\r\n});\r\n```\r\n\r\nCharacteristics:\r\n\r\n- Tests behavior users/callers care about\r\n- Uses public API only\r\n- Survives internal refactors\r\n- Describes WHAT, not HOW\r\n- One logical assertion per test\r\n\r\n## Bad Tests\r\n\r\n**Implementation-detail tests**: Coupled to internal structure.\r\n\r\n```typescript\r\n// BAD: Tests implementation details\r\ntest(\"checkout calls paymentService.process\", async () => {\r\n  const mockPayment = jest.mock(paymentService);\r\n  await checkout(cart, payment);\r\n  expect(mockPayment.process).toHaveBeenCalledWith(cart.total);\r\n});\r\n```\r\n\r\nRed flags:\r\n\r\n- Mocking internal collaborators\r\n- Testing private methods\r\n- Asserting on call counts/order\r\n- Test breaks when refactoring without behavior change\r\n- Test name describes HOW not WHAT\r\n- Verifying through external means instead of interface\r\n\r\n```typescript\r\n// BAD: Bypasses interface to verify\r\ntest(\"createUser saves to database\", async () => {\r\n  await createUser({ name: \"Alice\" });\r\n  const row = await db.query(\"SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ?\", [\"Alice\"]);\r\n  expect(row).toBeDefined();\r\n});\r\n\r\n// GOOD: Verifies through interface\r\ntest(\"createUser makes user retrievable\", async () => {\r\n  const user = await createUser({ name: \"Alice\" });\r\n  const retrieved = await getUser(user.id);\r\n  expect(retrieved.name).toBe(\"Alice\");\r\n});\r\n```\r\n\r\n**Tautological tests**: Expected value restates the implementation, so the test passes by construction.\r\n\r\n```typescript\r\n// BAD: Expected value is recomputed the way the code computes it\r\ntest(\"calculateTotal sums line items\", () => {\r\n  const items = [{ price: 10 }, { price: 5 }];\r\n  const expected = items.reduce((sum, i) => sum + i.price, 0);\r\n  expect(calculateTotal(items)).toBe(expected);\r\n});\r\n\r\n// GOOD: Expected value is an independent, known literal\r\ntest(\"calculateTotal sums line items\", () => {\r\n  expect(calculateTotal([{ price: 10 }, { price: 5 }])).toBe(15);\r\n});\r\n```\r\n# When to Mock\r\n\r\nMock at **system boundaries** only:\r\n\r\n- External APIs (payment, email, etc.)\r\n- Databases (sometimes - prefer test DB)\r\n- Time/randomness\r\n- File system (sometimes)\r\n\r\nDon't mock:\r\n\r\n- Your own classes/modules\r\n- Internal collaborators\r\n- Anything you control\r\n\r\n## Designing for Mockability\r\n\r\nAt system boundaries, design interfaces that are easy to mock:\r\n\r\n**1. Use dependency injection**\r\n\r\nPass external dependencies in rather than creating them internally:\r\n\r\n```typescript\r\n// Easy to mock\r\nfunction processPayment(order, paymentClient) {\r\n  return paymentClient.charge(order.total);\r\n}\r\n\r\n// Hard to mock\r\nfunction processPayment(order) {\r\n  const client = new StripeClient(process.env.STRIPE_KEY);\r\n  return client.charge(order.total);\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\n**2. Prefer SDK-style interfaces over generic fetchers**\r\n\r\nCreate specific functions for each external operation instead of one generic function with conditional logic:\r\n\r\n```typescript\r\n// GOOD: Each function is independently mockable\r\nconst api = {\r\n  getUser: (id) => fetch(`/users/${id}`),\r\n  getOrders: (userId) => fetch(`/users/${userId}/orders`),\r\n  createOrder: (data) => fetch('/orders', { method: 'POST', body: data }),\r\n};\r\n\r\n// BAD: Mocking requires conditional logic inside the mock\r\nconst api = {\r\n  fetch: (endpoint, options) => fetch(endpoint, options),\r\n};\r\n```\r\n\r\nThe SDK approach means:\r\n- Each mock returns one specific shape\r\n- No conditional logic in test setup\r\n- Easier to see which endpoints a test exercises\r\n- Type safety per endpoint\r\n"}}

construction.\\r\\n\\r\\n```typescript\\r\\n// BAD: Expected value is recomputed the way the code computes it\\r\\ntest(\\\"calculateTotal sums line items\\\", () => {\\r\\n  const items = [{ price: (sometimes)\\r\\n\\r\\nDon't mock:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Your own classes/modules\\r\\n- Internal collaborators\\r\\n- Anything you control\\r\\n\\r\\n## Designing for Mockability\\r\\n\\r\\nAt system boundaries, design interfaces that are easy to mock:\\r\\n\\r\\n**1. Avoid `any`.\r\n- Handle errors and asynchronous operations explicitly.\r\n- Validate external input.\r\n- Consider transaction boundaries and data consistency.\r\n- Add tests for new or changed behavior.\r\n- Never silently change existing API contracts.\r\n\r\n## Before Completing a Task\r\n\r\nRun applicable checks:\r\n\r\n1. Lint.\r\n2. Type checking.\r\n3. Relevant unit and integration tests.\r\n4. Build.\r\n\r\nIf a check cannot run, explain why.\r\n\r\n## Final Response\r\n\r\nSummarize:\r\n\r\n- What changed.\r\n- Important implementation decisions.\r\n- Tests and validation performed.\r\n- Known limitations or remaining work.\r\n\r\nDo not claim that a test, build, or validation passed unless it was actually executed.\r\n\r\n\r\n## Feature Development Workflow\r\n\r\nFor behavior-changing features, enhancements, significant refactors, and bug fixes, follow `docs/workflow-coding.md`. It defines the grilling confirmation gate, BDD scenario traceability, scaled feature artifacts, and the TDD cycle.\r\n# Feature Development Workflow\r\n\r\nUse this workflow for features, enhancements, significant refactors, and bug fixes that change behavior. Scale the documentation to the change, but keep the clarification, BDD, and TDD gates for behavior changes.\r\n\r\n## 1. Understand and clarify\r\n\r\nInspect the existing implementation, related tests, architecture, project context, applicable coding standards, and available test commands. Establish repository facts yourself before asking the user.\r\n\r\nFor behavior-changing work, invoke the `grilling` skill:\r\n\r\n- Start with a short clarification round for a straightforward change. Expand into a full design-tree interview when decisions are ambiguous, risky, or have competing solutions.\r\n- Ask all currently answerable questions in a round, number them, and give a recommended answer for each. Wait for the user's answers, then recompute the next question frontier.\r\n- Do not ask the user to discover facts available in the repository or environment.\r\n- When the frontier is settled, present a concise shared-understanding summary covering requirements, constraints, scenarios, design choices, and material test seams. Wait for explicit user confirmation before treating the specification as approved or implementing. If the user declines or asks to stop, stop.\r\n\r\n## 2. Specify and write BDD scenarios\r\n\r\nStore approved feature artifacts under `specs/<feature-name>/`. `.scratch/` may hold temporary discovery notes and issue-tracking tickets; promote the approved specification into `specs/` before implementation.\r\n\r\nFor a feature, enhancement, or significant change, create or update:\r\n\r\n- `spec.md`: requirements, constraints, acceptance criteria, and stable-ID Given/When/Then scenarios.\r\n- `design.md`: architecture, components, API contracts, data model, and material test seams.\r\n- `plan.md`: implementation approach and milestones.\r\n- `task.md`: ordered tasks and validation evidence.\r\n\r\nFor a narrow bug fix, use a concise `spec.md` for the expected behavior and relevant scenarios, plus `task.md` for implementation and test evidence. Add `design.md` or `plan.md` when the fix has material design or sequencing decisions. Expand the artifacts if the scope grows.\r\n\r\nTrace every acceptance criterion to one or more BDD scenarios. Include meaningful failure and boundary cases; do not create a separate scenario for every trivial variant. BDD scenarios describe observable behavior and are the source for implementation-level test coverage.\r\n\r\n## 3. Review before implementation\r\n\r\nConfirm that:\r\n\r\n- The user-approved understanding, requirements, and constraints are reflected in the spec.\r\n- Acceptance criteria and BDD scenarios are clear, observable, and traceable.\r\n- The design, public test seams, and test layers fit the architecture and have no unresolved material decisions.\r\n- Tasks are actionable and small enough for vertical implementation slices.\r\n\r\nResolve gaps with the user before implementation. Do not implement behavior outside the approved specification.\r\n\r\n## 4. Implement BDD-first with TDD\r\n\r\nUse BDD to define behavior, then TDD to implement it at the most appropriate test layer. Trace each scenario to automated verification, choosing the lowest practical layer that proves the behavior. Reserve end-to-end tests for journeys that need cross-boundary validation; a scenario does not require a one-to-one end-to-end test.\r\n\r\nWork in vertical slices, one behavior at a time:\r\n\r\n1. **Red:** Add a meaningful test for an approved behavior and run it. Confirm it fails because the behavior is missing or incorrect, not because of setup or environment failure.\r\n2. **Green:** Make the smallest production change that passes the test and relevant existing tests.\r\n3. **Refactor:** Improve the code while keeping the tests green.\r\n\r\nRecord the test layer, command, expected Red result, and Green result in `task.md`. If the Red test cannot be run, record the blocker and do not claim that the TDD cycle is complete. For non-behavioral edits, a new failing test is unnecessary; mechanical refactors still need characterization coverage for the behavior they preserve.\r\n\r\nFollow the applicable coding standards:\r\n\r\n- `docs/backend/coding.standard.md`\r\n- `docs/frontend/coding.standard.md`\r\n\r\n## 5. Verify and complete\r\n\r\n- Run relevant tests, lint, type-check, and build commands for the affected projects.\r\n- Verify each acceptance criterion against its BDD scenarios and test evidence.\r\n- Check for regressions and unintended behavior changes.\r\n- Keep the implementation, specification, design, plan, and task evidence synchronized.\r\n- Mark tasks complete only when their checks have actually run and passed.\r\n\r\nReport what changed, important decisions, actual validation results, and remaining limitations. Never claim a test or validation passed unless it was executed.\r\n"}}

Hợp đồng API và DTO Whitelist\r\n\r\n### DTO Bộ lọc Audit\r\n```typescript\r\nexport class AdminAuditFilterDto {\r\n  @IsOptional()\r\n  @IsInt()\r\n  @Min(1)\r\n  page: number = 1;\r\n\r\n  @IsOptional()\r\n  @IsInt()\r\n  @Min(1)\r\n  @Max(100)\r\n  pageSize: number = 20;\r\n\r\n  @IsOptional()\r\n  @IsUUID()\r\n  actorId?: string;\r\n\r\n  @IsOptional()\r\n  @IsEnum(['ADMIN', 'SYSTEM'])\r\n  actorType?: 'ADMIN' | 'SYSTEM';\r\n\r\n  @IsOptional()\r\n  @IsString()\r\n  @MaxLength(100)\r\n  action?: string;\r\n\r\n  @IsOptional()\r\n  @IsEnum(['USER', 'CONNECTOR', 'NODE_TYPE'])\r\n  targetType?: 'USER' | 'CONNECTOR' | 'NODE_TYPE';\r\n\r\n  @IsOptional()\r\n  @IsString()\r\n  targetId?: string;\r\n\r\n  @IsOptional()\r\n  @IsISO8601()\r\n  from?: string;\r\n\r\n  @IsOptional()\r\n  @IsISO8601()\r\n  to?: string;\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\n### Response DTO Chi tiết Audit Event\r\n```typescript\r\nexport interface AdminAuditEventDetailDto {\r\n  id: string;\r\n  actorType: 'ADMIN' | 'SYSTEM';\r\n  actorId: string | null;\r\n  actorName: string | null;\r\n  actorEmail: string | null;\r\n  action: string;\r\n  targetType: 'USER' | 'CONNECTOR' | 'NODE_TYPE';\r\n  targetId: string;\r\n  targetName?: string | null;\r\n  reason: string;\r\n  before: Record<string, unknown>;\r\n  after: Record<string, unknown>;\r\n  createdAt: string;\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\n## 3. Thiết kế Giao diện Frontend\r\n\r\n- `AuditEventsPage.tsx`:\r\n  - `AuditEventFilterBar.tsx`:\r\n    - Dropdown chọn `Action` (`USER_SUSPENDED`, `USER_REACTIVATED`, `USER_ROLE_CHANGED`, `ADMIN_BOOTSTRAPPED`, `CONNECTOR_POLICY_CHANGED`, `NODE_TYPE_STATUS_CHANGED`).\r\n    - Dropdown chọn `Target Type` (All, User, Connector, Node Type).\r\n    - Dropdown chọn `Actor Type` (All, Admin, System).\r\n    - Bộ chọn thời gian (Quick 24h, 7d, 30d, custom).\r\n  - `AuditEventTable.tsx`:\r\n    - Cột: Thời điểm (UTC & Local), Actor (Tên/Email hoặc SYSTEM badge), Hành động (Badge theo màu), Loại tài nguyên, ID tài nguyên, Lý do tóm tắt, Nút \"Xem chi tiết\".\r\n- `AuditDiffDialog.tsx`:\r\n  - Header: Tên hành động, Actor, Thời gian, Target ID.\r\n  - Khối lý do Admin: Hiển thị đầy đủ chuỗi reason trong callout box.\r\n  - Bảng đối chiếu Diff trực quan:\r\n    - Cột 1: Tên thuộc tính (Field name).\r\n    - Cột 2: Giá trị trước đó (Before) - highlight đỏ nhạt nếu bị xóa/tắt.\r\n    - Cột 3: Giá trị sau đó (After) - highlight xanh nhạt nếu được cập nhật/bật.\r\n- Hook: `useAdminAudit.ts` sử dụng TanStack Query với query keys `['admin', 'audit-events', filters]`.\r\n"}}

Yêu cầu Chức năng (Functional Requirements)\\r\\n\\r\\n### FR-AL-01: Phạm vi Ghi nhận Kiểm toán (Audit Logging Scope)\\r\\nMọi thao tác quản trị có hiệu lực làm thay đổi dữ liệu phải được ghi nhận vào `admin_audit_events` cùng database transaction với mutation nghiệp vụ:\\r\\n1. `USER_SUSPENDED`: Khóa tài khoản người dùng (G2 - Đã có).\\r\\n2. `USER_REACTIVATED`: Mở khóa tài khoản người dùng (G2 - Đã có).\\r\\n3. `USER_ROLE_CHANGED`: Đổi vai trò Client ↔ Admin (G2 - Đã có).\\r\\n4. `ADMIN_BOOTSTRAPPED`: Khởi tạo Admin đầu tiên qua lệnh CLI nội bộ (G1 - Đã có).\\r\\n5. `CONNECTOR_POLICY_CHANGED`: Thay đổi chính sách `allowNewCredentials` của connector (G4 - Mới).\\r\\n6. `NODE_TYPE_STATUS_CHANGED`: Thay đổi trạng thái `isCatalogVisible` hoặc `isExecutionAllowed` của node type (G5 - Mới).\\r\\n\\r\\n### FR-AL-02: Cấu trúc Bản ghi và Whitelist Trước/Sau (Before/After)\\r\\n- Bản ghi audit gồm: `id` (UUID), `actorType` (`ADMIN`, `SYSTEM`), `actorId` (UUID hoặc null), `action` (tên hành động), `targetType` (`USER`, `CONNECTOR`, `NODE_TYPE`), `targetId` (UUID hoặc key), `reason` (chuỗi lý do bắt buộc từ 5 đến 500 ký tự), `before` (JSON), `after` (JSON), `createdAt` (UTC timestamp).\\r\\n- **Nguyên tắc Whitelist Before/After**:\\r\\n  - Tuyệt đối không chụp toàn bộ object (snapshot dump).\\r\\n  - Chỉ lưu các trường trạng thái liên quan:\\r\\n    - User mutations: `{ isActive, role, revision }`.\\r\\n    - Connector policy mutations: `{ allowNewCredentials, revision }`.\\r\\n    - Node type status mutations: `{ isCatalogVisible, isExecutionAllowed, revision }`.\\r\\n    - Bootstrap: `{ role: 'ADMIN', isActive: true }`.\\r\\n\\r\\n### FR-AL-03: Danh sách và Bộ lọc Nhật ký Quản trị\\r\\n- API `GET /api/admin/audit-events`:\\r\\n  - **Bộ lọc**:\\r\\n    - `actorId`: Lọc theo ID quản trị viên thực hiện.\\r\\n    - `actorType`: Lọc theo `ADMIN` hoặc `SYSTEM`.\\r\\n    - `action`: Lọc theo tên hành động cụ thể.\\r\\n    - `targetType`: Lọc theo loại tài nguyên (`USER`, `CONNECTOR`, `NODE_TYPE`).\\r\\n    - `targetId`: Lọc theo ID tài nguyên mục tiêu.\\r\\n    - `from` và `to`: Khoảng thời gian nửa mở `[from, to)` (tối đa 90 ngày).\\r\\n  - Phân trang server-side (`page`, `pageSize`, mặc định 20, tối đa 100), sắp xếp giảm dần theo thời gian tạo (`createdAt desc`, `id desc`).\\r\\n  - Response danh sách bao gồm thông tin tóm tắt kèm tên/email của actor (nếu có).\\r\\n\\r\\n### FR-AL-04: Chi tiết Sự kiện và Đối chiếu Thay đổi (Diff Viewer)\\r\\n- API `GET /api/admin/audit-events/:id`:\\r\\n  - Trả về thông tin chi tiết sự kiện kiểm toán: Mã sự kiện, người thực hiện (tên, email), hành động, tài nguyên mục tiêu (loại, ID, tên nếu join được), thời điểm chính xác (UTC và local), lý do Admin đã nhập.\\r\\n  - Khối dữ liệu Before và After được hiển thị đối chiếu trực quan (Diff Viewer): Nổi bật các trường bị thay đổi (ví dụ: `isActive: true` -> `isActive: false`).\\r\\n\\r\\n### FR-AL-05: Tính Bất biến và Toàn vẹn (Immutability & Atomic Writes)\\r\\n- Bảng `admin_audit_events` hoàn toàn chỉ đọc: Backend tuyệt đối không cung cấp bất kỳ API nào để cập nhật (`PUT`/`PATCH`) hay xóa (`DELETE`) bản ghi audit.\\r\\n- Ghi nhận atomic: Nếu việc ghi bản ghi audit vào cơ sở dữ liệu gặp lỗi, toàn bộ transaction của mutation đó bắt buộc phải bị rollback; hệ thống không bao giờ ghi nhận thay đổi thành công mà thiếu bản ghi audit tương ứng.\\r\\n- Các thao tác no-op hoặc request bị từ chối do phân quyền / sai revision không được phát sinh bản ghi audit.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 3. Tiêu chí Nghiệm thu (Acceptance Criteria)\\r\\n- **AC-AL-01**: Admin tra cứu danh sách audit events lọc theo actor, action, target và thời gian chính xác; phân trang đúng.\\r\\n- **AC-AL-02**: Xem chi tiết audit event hiển thị đầy đủ thông tin actor, target, lý do và diff Before/After theo đúng whitelist.\\r\\n- **AC-AL-03**: Bảng audit events bất biến 100%; không có bất kỳ endpoint chỉnh sửa hoặc xóa nào.\\r\\n- **AC-AL-04**: Ghi audit thất bại làm rollback toàn bộ transaction mutation tương ứng.\\r\\n- **AC-AL-05**: Toàn bộ các thao tác thay đổi ở G1, G2, G4, G5 đều phát sinh bản ghi audit tương ứng với action chuẩn hóa.\\r\\n# Thiết kế: Trình tra cứu Nhật ký Quản trị (Audit Log Viewer)\\r\\n\\r\\nStatus: ready-for-agent (P1)\\r\\n\\r\\n## 1. Ranh giới Module và Phân tầng Kiến trúc\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Presentation**: `AdminController` trong `libs/admin/src/presentation`:\\r\\n  - `GET /api/admin/audit-events` -> `AdminReadQuery({ kind: 'auditEvents', filter })`\\r\\n  - `GET /api/admin/audit-events/:id` -> `AdminReadQuery({ kind: 'auditEvent', id })`\\r\\n- **Query Projection**:\\r\\n  - `AdminReadPort.auditEvents(filter: AdminAuditFilter)`\\r\\n  - `AdminReadPort.auditEvent(id: string)`\\r\\n  - Triển khai trong `PrismaAdminRead` (`libs/admin/src/infrastructure/prisma-admin-read.ts`):\\r\\n    - Truy vấn bảng `admin_audit_events`.\\r\\n    - Join với bảng `users` để lấy `name`, `email` của `actorId`.\\r\\n- **Infrastructure & Persistence**:\\r\\n  - Model `AdminAuditEvent` trong `prisma/schema.prisma` (đã có từ P0).\\r\\n  - Chỉ mục tối ưu: `@@index([createdAt, id])` và `@@index([targetId, createdAt])`.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 2. Hợp đồng API và DTO Whitelist\\r\\n\\r\\n### DTO Bộ lọc Audit\\r\\n```typescript\\r\\nexport class AdminAuditFilterDto {\\r\\n  @IsOptional()\\r\\n  @IsInt()\\r\\n  @Min(1)\\r\\n  page: number = 1;\\r\\n\\r\\n  @IsOptional()\\r\\n  @IsInt()\\r\\n  @Min(1)\\r\\n  @Max(100)\\r\\n  pageSize: number = 20;\\r\\n\\r\\n  @IsOptional()\\r\\n  @IsUUID()\\r\\n  actorId?: string;\\r\\n\\r\\n  @IsOptional()\\r\\n  @IsEnum(['ADMIN', 'SYSTEM'])\\r\\n  actorType?: 'ADMIN' | 'SYSTEM';\\r\\n\\r\\n  @IsOptional()\\r\\n  @IsString()\\r\\n  @MaxLength(100)\\r\\n  action?: string;\\r\\n\\r\\n  @IsOptional()\\r\\n  @IsEnum(['USER', 'CONNECTOR', 'NODE_TYPE'])\\r\\n  targetType?: 'USER' | 'CONNECTOR' | 'NODE_TYPE';\\r\\n\\r\\n  @IsOptional()\\r\\n  @IsString()\\r\\n  targetId?: string;\\r\\n\\r\\n  @IsOptional()\\r\\n  @IsISO8601()\\r\\n  from?: string;\\r\\n\\r\\n  @IsOptional()\\r\\n  @IsISO8601()\\r\\n  to?: string;\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n### Response DTO Chi tiết Audit Event\\r\\n```typescript\\r\\nexport interface AdminAuditEventDetailDto {\\r\\n  id: string;\\r\\n  actorType: 'ADMIN' | 'SYSTEM';\\r\\n  actorId: string | null;\\r\\n  actorName: string | null;\\r\\n  actorEmail: string | null;\\r\\n  action: string;\\r\\n  targetType: 'USER' | 'CONNECTOR' | 'NODE_TYPE';\\r\\n  targetId: string;\\r\\n  targetName?: string | null;\\r\\n  reason: string;\\r\\n  before: Record<string, unknown>;\\r\\n  after: Record<string, unknown>;\\r\\n  createdAt: string;\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## 3. Thiết kế Giao diện Frontend\\r\\n\\r\\n- `AuditEventsPage.tsx`:\\r\\n  - `AuditEventFilterBar.tsx`:\\r\\n    - Dropdown chọn `Action` (`USER_SUSPENDED`, `USER_REACTIVATED`, `USER_ROLE_CHANGED`, `ADMIN_BOOTSTRAPPED`, `CONNECTOR_POLICY_CHANGED`, `NODE_TYPE_STATUS_CHANGED`).\\r\\n    - Dropdown chọn `Target Type` (All, User, Connector, Node Type).\\r\\n    - Dropdown chọn `Actor Type` (All, Admin, System).\\r\\n    - Bộ chọn thời gian (Quick 24h, 7d, 30d, custom).\\r\\n  - `AuditEventTable.tsx`:\\r\\n    - Cột: Thời điểm (UTC & Local), Actor (Tên/Email hoặc SYSTEM badge), Hành động (Badge theo màu), Loại tài nguyên, ID tài nguyên, Lý do tóm tắt, Nút \\\"Xem chi tiết\\\".\\r\\n- `AuditDiffDialog.tsx`:\\r\\n  - Header: Tên hành động, Actor, Thời gian, Target ID.\\r\\n  - Khối lý do Admin: Hiển thị đầy đủ chuỗi reason trong callout box.\\r\\n  - Bảng đối chiếu Diff trực quan:\\r\\n    - Cột 1: Tên thuộc tính (Field name).\\r\\n    - Cột 2: Giá trị trước đó (Before) - highlight đỏ nhạt nếu bị xóa/tắt.\\r\\n    - Cột 3: Giá trị sau đó (After) - highlight xanh nhạt nếu được cập nhật/bật.\\r\\n- Hook: `useAdminAudit.ts` sử dụng TanStack Query với query keys `['admin', 'audit-events', filters]`.\\r\\n\"}}"

\"created_at\");\r\nexport interface NodeTypePolicySnapshot {\r\n  nodeTypeKey: string;\r\n  isCatalogVisible: boolean;\r\n  isExecutionAllowed: boolean;\r\n  revision: number;\r\n  updatedAt: Date;\r\n}\r\nexport interface ChangeNodeTypeStatusParams {\r\n  nodeTypeKey: string;\r\n  isCatalogVisible?: boolean;\r\n  isExecutionAllowed?: boolean;\r\n  reason: string;\r\n  expectedRevision: number;\r\n  adminId: string;\r\n}\r\nexport class NodeTypePolicyError extends Error {\r\n  constructor(\r\n    readonly code:\r\n      'INVALID_NODE_TYPE_POLICY' | 'STALE_REVISION' | 'NODE_TYPE_NOT_FOUND',\r\n    message: string,\r\n  ) {\r\n    super(message);\r\n  }\r\n}\r\nexport class NodeTypeDisabledError extends Error {\r\n  readonly code = 'NODE_TYPE_DISABLED';\r\n  constructor(key: string) {\r\n    super(`Node type ${key} is disabled by the platform administrator`);\r\n  }\r\n}\r\nexport function planNodeTypeStatusChange(\r\n  current: NodeTypePolicySnapshot,\r\n  params: ChangeNodeTypeStatusParams,\r\n) {\r\n  const reason = typeof params.reason === 'string' ? params.reason.trim() : '';\r\n  const flags = [params.isCatalogVisible, params.isExecutionAllowed];\r\n  if (\r\n    reason.length < 5 ||\r\n    reason.length > 500 ||\r\n    !Number.isInteger(params.expectedRevision) ||\r\n    params.expectedRevision < 0 ||\r\n    flags.every((flag) => flag === undefined) ||\r\n    flags.some((flag) => flag !== undefined && typeof flag !== 'boolean')\r\n  ) {\r\n    throw new NodeTypePolicyError(\r\n      'INVALID_NODE_TYPE_POLICY',\r\n      'Provide at least one boolean flag, a nonnegative integer revision and a reason of 5–500 characters',\r\n    );\r\n  }\r\n  if (current.revision !== params.expectedRevision)\r\n    throw new NodeTypePolicyError(\r\n      'STALE_REVISION',\r\n      'Policy changed; reload before continuing',\r\n    );\r\n  const isCatalogVisible = params.isCatalogVisible ?? current.isCatalogVisible;\r\n  const isExecutionAllowed =\r\n    params.isExecutionAllowed ?? current.isExecutionAllowed;\r\n  const changed =\r\n    isCatalogVisible !== current.isCatalogVisible ||\r\n    isExecutionAllowed !== current.isExecutionAllowed;\r\n  return {\r\n    ...current,\r\n    isCatalogVisible,\r\n    isExecutionAllowed,\r\n    revision: current.revision + (changed ? 1 : 0),\r\n    changed,\r\n    reason: params.reason.trim(),\r\n  };\r\n}\r\n"}}

không lưu mật khẩu, token, secret.\r\n  - `createdAt`: Thời điểm phát sinh sự kiện (UTC).\r\n- **Giao diện Tra cứu (Audit Log Viewer)**:\r\n  - Danh sách sự kiện kiểm toán với phân trang server-side, sắp xếp mới nhất trước (`createdAt desc`, `id desc`).\r\n  - Bộ lọc đa tiêu chí: Lọc theo `actorId`, `actorType`, `action`, `targetType`, `targetId`, và khoảng thời gian `[from, to)` (tối đa 90 ngày).\r\n  - Chi tiết sự kiện: Hiển thị thông tin người thực hiện (tên, email nếu có), hành động, thời điểm, lý do, và bảng đối chiếu trực quan các trường thay đổi (Diff Before vs After).\r\n- **Tính Bất biến và Toàn vẹn**:\r\n  - Bảng audit hoàn toàn chỉ đọc; backend không cung cấp bất kỳ API nào để cập nhật (`PUT`/`PATCH`) hay xóa (`DELETE`) bản ghi audit.\r\n  - Nếu việc ghi audit thất bại, toàn bộ transaction của mutation đó phải bị rollback; hệ thống không bao giờ ghi nhận thay đổi thành công mà thiếu bản ghi audit tương ứng.\r\n  - Các request bị từ chối do phân quyền, sai revision (`409`), hoặc các thao tác no-op không làm phát sinh bản ghi audit.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 11. Các câu hỏi mở (Open Questions)\r\nspecs/admin-management/analysis.md-100-\r\nspecs/admin-management/analysis.md-101-1. **Phạm vi đếm workflow sử dụng Node Type**: Có nên đếm cả trong bản nháp (`WorkflowDraft`) hay chỉ đếm các phiên bản đã phát hành (`WorkflowVersion` published)?\r\nspecs/admin-management/analysis.md-102-   - *Đề xuất*: Đếm riêng biệt 2 chỉ số: số workflow đã publish (ảnh hưởng runtime) và số workflow nháp (ảnh hưởng người đang thiết kế).\r\nspecs/admin-management/analysis.md-103-2. **Cơ chế xử lý khi node bị tắt thực thi (`isExecutionAllowed = false`)**: Khi một node đang chạy bị chặn, workflow nên chuyển trạng thái `FAILED` ngay lập tức hay chuyển sang nhánh error handling (nếu có)?\r\nspecs/admin-management/analysis.md-104-   - *Đề xuất*: Đánh dấu node log là `FAILED` với mã lỗi chuẩn `NODE_TYPE_DISABLED`; execution chuyển `FAILED` theo quy tắc xử lý lỗi hiện có của engine.\r\nStore approved feature artifacts under `specs/<feature-name>/`. `.scratch/` may hold temporary discovery notes and issue-tracking tickets; promote the approved specification into `specs/` before implementation.\r\n\r\nFor a feature, enhancement, or significant change, create or update:\r\n\r\n- `spec.md`: requirements, constraints, acceptance criteria, and stable-ID Given/When/Then scenarios.\r\n- `design.md`: architecture, components, API contracts, data model, and material test seams.\r\n- `plan.md`: implementation approach and milestones.\r\n- `task.md`: ordered tasks and validation evidence.\r\n\r\nFor a narrow bug fix, use a concise `spec.md` for the expected behavior and relevant scenarios, plus `task.md` for implementation and test evidence. Add `design.md` or `plan.md` when the fix has material design or sequencing decisions. Expand the artifacts if the scope grows.\r\n\r\nTrace every acceptance criterion to one or more BDD scenarios. Include meaningful failure and boundary cases; do not create a separate scenario for every trivial variant. BDD scenarios describe observable behavior and are the source for implementation-level test coverage.\r\n\r\n## 3. Review before implementation\r\n\r\nConfirm that:\r\n\r\n- The user-approved understanding, requirements, and constraints are reflected in the spec.\r\n- Acceptance criteria and BDD scenarios are clear, observable, and traceable.\r\n- The design, public test seams, and test layers fit the architecture and have no unresolved material decisions.\r\n- Tasks are actionable and small enough for vertical implementation slices.\r\n\r\nResolve gaps with the user before implementation. Do not implement behavior outside the approved specification.\r\n\r\n## 4. Implement BDD-first with TDD\r\n\r\nUse BDD to define behavior, then TDD to implement it at the most appropriate test layer. Trace each scenario to automated verification, choosing the lowest practical layer that proves the behavior. Reserve end-to-end tests for journeys that need cross-boundary validation; a scenario does not require a one-to-one end-to-end test.\r\n\r\nWork in vertical slices, one behavior at a time:\r\n\r\n1. **Red:** Add a meaningful test for an approved behavior and run it. Confirm it fails because the behavior is missing or incorrect, not because of setup or environment failure.\r\n2. **Green:** Make the smallest production change that passes the test and relevant existing tests.\r\n3. **Refactor:** Improve the code while keeping the tests green.\r\n\r\nRecord the test layer, command, expected Red result, and Green result in `task.md`. If the Red test cannot be run, record the blocker and do not claim that the TDD cycle is complete. Xử lý Đồng thời, Chống Race Condition và Giao dịch Database\r\n\r\n### 4.1. Hệ thống Khóa Quản trị (PostgreSQL Advisory Locks)\r\nĐể chống race condition giữa nhiều Admin hoặc giữa Admin và Client, hệ thống sử dụng các Transaction Advisory Lock riêng biệt:\r\n- **Tài khoản người dùng**: `SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(7261101)`\r\n- **Chính sách Connector**: `SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(7261102)`\r\n- **Chính sách Node Type**: `SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(7261103)`\r\n\r\n### 4.2. Xử lý Race Condition tại luồng tạo Credential (G4)\r\nKhi người dùng bấm \"Connect with Google\":\r\n1. Bắt đầu OAuth (`/api/integrations/google/auth`): Kiểm tra `allowNewCredentials`. Nếu `false`, từ chối ngay.\r\n2. Hoàn tất OAuth (`/api/integrations/google/callback`):\r\n   - Mở database transaction.\r\n   - Lấy advisory lock hoặc row-lock `SELECT ... FROM connector_policies WHERE connector_id = $1 FOR UPDATE`.\r\n   - Kiểm tra lại `allowNewCredentials`.\r\n   - Nếu `false`: Rollback transaction, hủy lưu trữ credential, trả về lỗi `409 Conflict` (mã `CONNECTOR_NEW_CREDENTIALS_DISABLED`).\r\n   - Nếu `true`: Lưu `ConnectorCredential`, commit transaction.\r\n   *Cơ chế này áp dụng tương tự cho API Key credential và Package OAuth2.*\r\n\r\n### 4.3. Xử lý Tính tương thích và Chặn Runtime ở Node Type (G5)\r\n1. **Designer Palette Filtering**: `NodeTypesController.getNodeTypes()` truy vấn kết hợp bảng `node_type_definitions` và `node_type_policies`:\r\n   - Lọc bỏ các node có `isCatalogVisible === false`.\r\n2. **Runtime Execution Enforcement (`NodeRunner`)**:\r\n   - Khi engine nạp node để thực thi: `NodeRunner` kiểm tra cờ `isExecutionAllowed` của `nodeKey`.\r\n   - Nếu `isExecutionAllowed === false`: \r\n     - Không gọi `executor.execute()`.\r\n     - Ghi nhận `ExecutionNodeLog` với status `FAILED`, `errorCode = 'NODE_TYPE_DISABLED'`.\r\n     - Ném `NodeTypeDisabledException` để workflow engine xử lý theo kịch bản lỗi chuẩn hóa.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 5. Thiết kế Giao diện Frontend (UI Architecture)\r\n\r\nTổ chức trong `frontend/src/features/admin`:\r\n\r\n```\r\nfrontend/src/features/admin/\r\n├── components/\r\n| `/admin/executions` | Giám sát Execution | Bộ lọc đa chiều (owner, workflow, execution ID, status, trigger, time), bảng danh sách metadata an toàn |\r\n| `/admin/executions/:id` | Chi tiết Execution | Metadata execution, bảng tiến trình và kết quả từng node (status, timing, mã lỗi an toàn; không payload) |\r\n| `/admin/audit-events` | Nhật ký Quản trị | Danh sách sự kiện kiểm toán, bộ lọc actor/action/target/thời gian, dialog xem chi tiết diff Before/After |\r\n\r\nChuẩn mực UI:\r\n- Sử dụng thư viện **shadcn/ui** (`@/components/ui/*`) và **Tailwind CSS v4**. Tuyệt đối không tự viết lại các HTML element cơ bản (dialogs, buttons, tables, badges, dropdowns, inputs).\r\n- Mọi dialog mutation đều phải yêu cầu nhập lý do, hiển thị tóm tắt tác động trước/sau và xác nhận rõ ràng trước khi gửi request.\r\n- Mọi trang danh sách đều hỗ trợ trạng thái loading skeleton, empty state, error state có nút retry và visible-only polling.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## 12. Xử lý Đồng thời, Chống Race Condition và Giao dịch Database\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.1. Hệ thống Khóa Quản trị (PostgreSQL Advisory Locks)\\r\\nĐể chống race condition giữa nhiều Admin hoặc giữa Admin và Client, hệ thống sử dụng các Transaction Advisory Lock riêng biệt:\\r\\n- **Tài khoản người dùng**: `SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(7261101)`\\r\\n- **Chính sách Connector**: `SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(7261102)`\\r\\n- **Chính sách Node Type**: `SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(7261103)`\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.2. Xử lý Race Condition tại luồng tạo Credential (G4)\\r\\nKhi người dùng bấm \\\"Connect with Google\\\":\\r\\n1. Bắt đầu OAuth (`/api/integrations/google/auth`): Kiểm tra `allowNewCredentials`. Nếu `false`, từ chối ngay.\\r\\n2. Hoàn tất OAuth (`/api/integrations/google/callback`):\\r\\n   - Mở database transaction.\\r\\n   - Lấy advisory lock hoặc row-lock `SELECT ... FROM connector_policies WHERE connector_id = $1 FOR UPDATE`.\\r\\n   - Kiểm tra lại `allowNewCredentials`.\\r\\n   - Nếu `false`: Rollback transaction, hủy lưu trữ credential, trả về lỗi `409 Conflict` (mã `CONNECTOR_NEW_CREDENTIALS_DISABLED`).\\r\\n   - Nếu `true`: Lưu `ConnectorCredential`, commit transaction.\\r\\n   *Cơ chế này áp dụng tương tự cho API Key credential và Package OAuth2.*\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.3. Xử lý Tính tương thích và Chặn Runtime ở Node Type (G5)\\r\\n1. **Designer Palette Filtering**: `NodeTypesController.getNodeTypes()` truy vấn kết hợp bảng `node_type_definitions` và `node_type_policies`:\\r\\n   - Lọc bỏ các node có `isCatalogVisible === false`.\\r\\n2. **Runtime Execution Enforcement (`NodeRunner`)**:\\r\\n   - Khi engine nạp node để thực thi: `NodeRunner` kiểm tra cờ `isExecutionAllowed` của `nodeKey`.\\r\\n   - Nếu `isExecutionAllowed === false`: \\r\\n     - Không gọi `executor.execute()`.\\r\\n     - Ghi nhận `ExecutionNodeLog` với status `FAILED`, `errorCode = 'NODE_TYPE_DISABLED'`.\\r\\n     - Ném `NodeTypeDisabledException` để workflow engine xử lý theo kịch bản lỗi chuẩn hóa.\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## 5. Thiết kế Giao diện Frontend (UI Architecture)\\r\\n\\r\\nTổ chức trong `frontend/src/features/admin`:\\r\\n\\r\\n```\\r\\nfrontend/src/features/admin/\\r\\n├── components/\\r\\n| `/admin/executions` | Giám sát Execution | Bộ lọc đa chiều (owner, workflow, execution ID, status, trigger, time), bảng danh sách metadata an toàn |\\r\\n| `/admin/executions/:id` | Chi tiết Execution | Metadata execution, bảng tiến trình và kết quả từng node (status, timing, mã lỗi an toàn; không payload) |\\r\\n| `/admin/audit-events` | Nhật ký Quản trị | Danh sách sự kiện kiểm toán, bộ lọc actor/action/target/thời gian, dialog xem chi tiết diff Before/After |\\r\\n\\r\\nChuẩn mực UI:\\r\\n- Sử dụng thư viện **shadcn/ui** (`@/components/ui/*`) và **Tailwind CSS v4**. Tuyệt đối không tự viết lại các HTML element cơ bản (dialogs, buttons, tables, badges, dropdowns, inputs).\\r\\n- Mọi dialog mutation đều phải yêu cầu nhập lý do, hiển thị tóm tắt tác động trước/sau và xác nhận rõ ràng trước khi gửi request.\\r\\n- Mọi trang danh sách đều hỗ trợ trạng thái loading skeleton, empty state, error state có nút retry và visible-only polling.\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## 12. Phân biệt `false`, `0`, `null` và thuộc tính không được ghi nhận; revision/key giữ nguyên không được highlight như thay đổi. Before/after và reason cần render như text, không chèn HTML hoặc dump snapshot tùy ý.\r\n\r\nNguồn yêu cầu: [G7 spec, FR-AL-02/04](spec.md), [G7 design, Diff Viewer](design.md). Quy tắc missing/null/highlight là đề xuất, hiện chưa có scenario tương ứng.\r\n\r\n**Query và thời gian.** from/to là khoảng nửa mở theo createdAt, tối đa 90 ngày. G7 chưa ghi mặc định khi bỏ một/hai mốc, validation from >= to, timezone bắt buộc, cách kết hợp filter và exact target lookup. Đề xuất AND, default 7 ngày, timestamp có timezone, detail ID không bị giới hạn bởi range list. Giới hạn độ dài range không đồng nghĩa xóa lịch sử quá 90 ngày.\r\n\r\nNguồn: [G7 spec, FR-AL-03](spec.md), [Admin spec, mục 12](../spec.md). Các mặc định nói trên cần được xác nhận, không phải yêu cầu đã có của G7.\r\n\r\n**Polling và UI states.** Admin spec chung yêu cầu visible-only polling cho list và loading/empty/error có retry; G7 chưa định interval hoặc policy cho detail dialog. Có thể reuse pattern G6, đề xuất list 30 giây khi visible; detail tải khi mở, không cần polling bản ghi bất biến. Nút retry tải lại chỉ gọi GET.\r\n\r\nNguồn: [Admin spec, chuẩn mực UI](../spec.md), [G7 design, useAdminAudit](design.md), [hook G6](../../../frontend/src/features/admin/hooks/useAdminExecutions.ts).\r\n\r\n**Phạm vi bất biến.** Migrations được đối chiếu mới có tạo bảng/index, chưa có trigger hoặc phân quyền database để ngăn UPDATE/DELETE audit. Không cung cấp HTTP mutation là yêu cầu có thể nghiệm thu ở API; chưa thể gọi database hiện tại là append-only/chống tamper. Nếu cần bảo vệ cả database, phải chốt thêm ranh giới quyền database và chính sách vận hành.\r\n\r\nNguồn: [migration Admin P0](../../../monolith-backend/prisma/migrations/20261114000000_admin_p0/migration.sql), [schema](../../../monolith-backend/prisma/schema.prisma), [G7 spec, FR-AL-05](spec.md).\r\n\r\n## 6. Các điểm cần chốt trước triển khai\r\n\r\n| Điểm chưa thống nhất | Bằng chứng | Hướng đề xuất |\r\n| --- | --- | --- |\r\n| targetId UUID hay key | Spec nói UUID/key; schema là UUID, G5 ghi definition.id | Giữ UUID, metadata key riêng; không đổi lịch sử âm thầm |\r\n| User revision thiếu; node key thừa theo whitelist G7 | Writer hiện tại khác FR-AL-02 | Chốt per-action whitelist và cách hiển thị dữ liệu cũ |\r\n| Actor/target tên hiện tại hay lịch sử | Design join live data, event chưa snapshot tên | Ghi rõ provenance, null fallback, bảo toàn event |\r\n| Actor ID và target ID chưa có control UI | Spec/API có hai filter; design filter bar không liệt kê | Bổ sung picker/UUID input và reset page khi đổi filter |\r\n| Action string tự do hay enum | DTO IsString; task nói enum, UI liệt kê sáu action | Chốt sáu action cho filter; quy tắc dữ liệu/action không nhận diện |\r\n| DTO chưa đủ validation | Thiếu numeric transform; IsEnum dùng array; targetId không giới hạn | Reuse PageDto/IsIn, validate UUID/range/length tại HTTP |\r\n| Default range và polling | G7 chỉ max90 ngày; parent yêu cầu polling list | Default/timezone/interval/lifecycle phải có scenario |\r\n| “Bất biến 100%” ở phạm vi nào | FR-AL-05 mô tả không API sửa/xóa | Nghiệm thu quyền ghi qua API; DB chống tamper là quyết định riêng nếu cần |\r\n| G7.3/tài liệu cha còn mô tả audit G4/G5 chưa có | Source đã có hai writer | Đồng bộ checklist theo hiện trạng, không implement trùng |\r\n| Nguồn yêu cầu SRS | G7 dẫn FR-AD-05 (đổi role), SRS audit là FR-AD-11 | Sửa mapping nguồn trước phê duyệt spec |\r\n\r\nNguồn: [G7 spec/design/task](spec.md), [SRS](../../../docs/srs.md), [schema](../../../monolith-backend/prisma/schema.prisma) và writers ở mục 3. | Chức năng | Hành vi yêu cầu |
|---|---|
| Danh sách | Lọc theo actor, action, target và thời gian; phân trang 20–100 dòng; mới nhất trước |
| Chi tiết | Hiển thị người thực hiện, tài nguyên, lý do, thời điểm UTC/local |
| Diff | So sánh Before/After theo whitelist, làm nổi bật trường thay đổi |
| Toàn vẹn | Audit cùng transaction với mutation; lỗi ghi audit phải rollback; no-op không tạo event |
| Quyền truy cập | Admin được đọc; không có API sửa/xóa audit |

**Hiện trạng:** code đã có writer cho đủ sáu action: khóa/mở khóa tài khoản, đổi role, bootstrap Admin, đổi connector policy và node policy. API đọc và UI G7 chưa có; checklist G7.3 đang mô tả hiện trạng cũ.

Các điểm quan trọng cần chốt:

- **Target ID:** spec cho phép UUID/key, nhưng database lưu UUID; node audit dùng `definition.id`.

- **Tên actor/target:** join chỉ lấy tên hiện tại; cần fallback khi không tìm thấy metadata.
- **Bất biến:** không có HTTP sửa/xóa chưa đồng nghĩa database đã chống UPDATE/DELETE.
- **Contract còn thiếu:** default thời gian, polling, control actor/target và validation action chưa thống nhất.

Đề xuất mở rộng CQRS Admin hiện có, hoàn thiện list → detail/diff → UI. Báo cáo có **12 BDD đề xuất** và chỉ ra khoảng trống kiểm thử rollback connector bằng PostgreSQL.

Semantic native HTML is appropriate.\r\n- Extend or compose existing components instead of copying their implementation.\r\n- Use Tailwind utilities for ordinary layout and styling. Add CSS modules or standalone CSS when styles are complex, reusable, or clearer outside class strings.\r\n- Avoid arbitrary values when a design token or existing spacing/color scale fits.\r\n- Do not use color as the only way to communicate status.\r\n- Interactive elements must be keyboard accessible and expose accessible names and states.\r\n- Use buttons for actions and links for navigation.\r\n- Use correct heading hierarchy, labels, landmarks, and table semantics.\r\n- Dialogs and popovers must manage focus and support keyboard dismissal according to their interaction pattern.\r\n- Do not remove focus indicators without providing an accessible replacement.\r\n- Prefer accessible Testing Library queries (`getByRole`, `getByLabelText`) over CSS selectors.\r\n\r\n## 10. Never leave it empty.\r\n- Cancellation and expected control-flow outcomes should not be reported as unexpected errors.\r\n\r\n## 12. Async behavior and real-time updates\r\n\r\n- Handle loading, cancellation, retries, and component unmounting deliberately.\r\n- Avoid fire-and-forget promises. Await them, return them, or explicitly handle rejection.\r\n- For SSE or WebSocket clients, define connection lifecycle, reconnect policy, event validation, deduplication, and terminal-state behavior.\r\n- Clean up subscriptions and listeners when their owner unmounts.\r\n- Do not assume events arrive exactly once or in order unless the server contract guarantees it.\r\n- Keep polling as a deliberate fallback with bounded frequency and a clear stop condition.\r\n- Do not log credentials, tokens, personal data, or full sensitive payloads.\r\n\r\n## 13. Performance\r\n\r\n- Measure before optimizing.\r\n- Avoid unnecessary global state subscriptions and broad query invalidations.\r\n- Paginate or virtualize genuinely large collections.\r\n- Debounce user input only when it improves the interaction and define when the pending value is committed.\r\n- Lazy-load large route-level or editor-only dependencies where beneficial.\r\n"}}

Add CSS modules or standalone CSS when styles are complex, reusable, or clearer outside class strings.\\r\\n- Avoid arbitrary values when a design token or existing spacing/color scale fits.\\r\\n- Do not use color as the only way to communicate status.\\r\\n- Interactive elements must be keyboard accessible and expose accessible names and states.\\r\\n- Use buttons for actions and links for navigation.\\r\\n- Use correct heading hierarchy, labels, landmarks, and table semantics.\\r\\n- Dialogs and popovers must manage focus and support keyboard dismissal according to their interaction pattern.\\r\\n- Do not remove focus indicators without providing an accessible replacement.\\r\\n- Prefer accessible Testing Library queries (`getByRole`, `getByLabelText`) over CSS selectors.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 10. React Flow and workflow designer\\r\\n\\r\\n- Keep custom node components separate from workflow execution/business rules.\\r\\n- Keep node rendering, node configuration forms, and node metadata distinct where this improves cohesion.\\r\\n- Use stable node and edge identifiers.\\r\\n- Avoid mutating React Flow node/edge objects directly; use the supported state update APIs.\\r\\n- Keep canvas-only transient state in the designer store, not in persisted workflow definitions unless it is part of the domain contract.\\r\\n- Validate workflow structure on the backend as well as in the UI.\\r\\n- Handle large canvases carefully; avoid unnecessary updates to every node when one node changes.\\r\\n- Document any custom connection, selection, or keyboard interaction that differs from React Flow defaults.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 11. Error, loading, and empty states\\r\\n\\r\\nEvery asynchronous user-facing view must intentionally handle the states relevant to its operation:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Initial loading\\r\\n- Empty result\\r\\n- Success\\r\\n- Recoverable error\\r\\n- Permission/authorization failure\\r\\n- Pending mutation or submission\\r\\n\\r\\nRules:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Show actionable, understandable feedback; do not expose stack traces or internal server details.\\r\\n- Preserve useful context when an action fails.\\r\\n- Use the shared notification/error presentation where available.\\r\\n- Do not show duplicate notifications for the same error at multiple layers.\\r\\n- A `catch` block must handle, enrich, or rethrow the error. Never leave it empty.\\r\\n- Cancellation and expected control-flow outcomes should not be reported as unexpected errors.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 12. Async behavior and real-time updates\\r\\n\\r\\n- Handle loading, cancellation, retries, and component unmounting deliberately.\\r\\n- Avoid fire-and-forget promises. Await them, return them, or explicitly handle rejection.\\r\\n- For SSE or WebSocket clients, define connection lifecycle, reconnect policy, event validation, deduplication, and terminal-state behavior.\\r\\n- Clean up subscriptions and listeners when their owner unmounts.\\r\\n- Do not assume events arrive exactly once or in order unless the server contract guarantees it.\\r\\n- Keep polling as a deliberate fallback with bounded frequency and a clear stop condition.\\r\\n- Do not log credentials, tokens, personal data, or full sensitive payloads.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 13. Use when the user says \\\"diagnose\\\"/\\\"debug this\\\", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Diagnosing Bugs\\r\\n\\r\\nA discipline for hard bugs. Skip phases only when explicitly justified.\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen exploring the codebase, read `CONTEXT.md` (if it exists) to get a clear mental model of the relevant modules, and check ADRs in the area you're touching.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Redact\\r\\n\\r\\nThis skill has you show commands, outputs and captured artifacts. **Redact every secret first**: write `<REDACTED>` in its place. Build loops against env vars, so the credential stays in the environment rather than in what you show. Captured artifacts carry auth headers: quote only the lines that carry the signal.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf the redacted output is not enough to diagnose the bug, say so and ask the user.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Phase 1: Build a feedback loop\\r\\n\\r\\n**This is the skill.** Everything else is mechanical. If you have a **tight** pass/fail signal for the bug (one that goes red on _this_ bug), you will find the cause; bisection, hypothesis-testing, and instrumentation all just consume it. If you don't have one, no amount of staring at code will save you.\\r\\n\\r\\nSpend disproportionate effort here. **Be aggressive. Be creative. Refuse to give up.**\\r\\n\\r\\n### Ways to construct one, in roughly this order\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Failing test** at whatever seam reaches the bug: unit, integration, e2e.\\r\\n2. **Curl / HTTP script** against a running dev server.\\r\\n3. **CLI invocation** with a fixture input, diffing stdout against a known-good snapshot.\\r\\n4. **Headless browser script** (Playwright / Puppeteer) that drives the UI and asserts on DOM/console/network.\\r\\n5. **Replay a captured trace.** Save a real network request / payload / event log to disk; replay it through the code path in isolation.\\r\\n6. **Throwaway harness.** Spin up a minimal subset of the system (one service, mocked deps) that exercises the bug code path with a single function call.\\r\\n7. **Property / fuzz loop.** If the bug is \\\"sometimes wrong output\\\", run 1000 random inputs and look for the failure mode.\\r\\n8. **Bisection harness.** If the bug appeared between two known states (commit, dataset, version), automate \\\"boot at state X, check, repeat\\\" so you can `git bisect run` it.\\r\\n9. **Differential loop.** Run the same input through old-version vs new-version (or two configs) and diff outputs.\\r\\n10. **HITL bash script.** Last resort. If a human must click, drive _them_ with `scripts/hitl-loop.template.sh` so the loop is still structured. Captured output feeds back to you.\\r\\n\\r\\nBuild the right feedback loop, and the bug is 90% fixed.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Tighten the loop\\r\\n\\r\\nTreat the loop as a product. Once you have _a_ loop, **tighten** it:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Can I make it faster? (Cache setup, skip unrelated init, narrow the test scope.)\\r\\n- Can I make the signal sharper? (Assert on the specific symptom, not \\\"didn't crash\\\".)\\r\\n- Can I make it more deterministic? (Pin time, seed RNG, isolate filesystem, freeze network.)\\r\\n\\r\\nA 30-second flaky loop is barely better than no loop; a 2-second deterministic one is tight, a debugging superpower.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Non-deterministic bugs\\r\\n\\r\\nThe goal is not a clean repro but a **higher reproduction rate**. Loop the trigger 100×, parallelise, add stress, narrow timing windows, inject sleeps. A 50%-flake bug is debuggable; 1% is not, so keep raising the rate until it's debuggable.\\r\\n\\r\\n### When you genuinely cannot build a loop\\r\\n\\r\\nStop and say so explicitly. List what you tried. Ask the user for: (a) access to whatever environment reproduces it, (b) a redacted captured artifact (HAR file, log dump, core dump, screen recording with timestamps), or (c) permission to add temporary production instrumentation. Do **not** proceed to hypothesise without a loop.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Completion criterion: a tight loop that goes red\\r\\n\\r\\nPhase 1 is done when the loop is **tight** and **red-capable**: you can name **one command** (a script path, a test invocation, a curl) that you have **already run at least once** (show the invocation and its output, redacted), and that is:\\r\\n\\r\\n- [ ] **Red-capable**: it drives the actual bug code path and asserts the **user's exact symptom**, so it can go red on this bug and green once fixed. Not \\\"runs without erroring\\\"; it must be able to _catch this specific bug_.\\r\\n- [ ] **Deterministic**: same verdict every run (flaky bugs: a pinned, high reproduction rate, per above).\\r\\n- [ ] **Fast**: seconds, not minutes.\\r\\n- [ ] **Agent-runnable**: you can run it unattended; a human in the loop only via `scripts/hitl-loop.template.sh`.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf you catch yourself reading code to build a theory before this command exists, **stop: jumping straight to a hypothesis is the exact failure this skill prevents.** No red-capable command, no Phase 2.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Phase 2: Reproduce + minimise\\r\\n\\r\\nRun the loop. Watch it go red as the bug appears.\\r\\n\\r\\nConfirm:\\r\\n\\r\\n- [ ] The loop produces the failure mode the **user** described, not a different failure that happens to be nearby. Wrong bug = wrong fix.\\r\\n- [ ] The failure is reproducible across multiple runs (or, for non-deterministic bugs, reproducible at a high enough rate to debug against).\\r\\n- [ ] You have captured the exact symptom (error message, wrong output, slow timing) so later phases can verify the fix actually addresses it.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Minimise\\r\\n\\r\\nOnce it's red, shrink the repro to the **smallest scenario that still goes red**. Cut inputs, callers, config, data, and steps **one at a time**, re-running the loop after each cut, and keep only what's load-bearing for the failure.\\r\\n\\r\\nWhy bother: a minimal repro shrinks the hypothesis space in Phase 3 (fewer moving parts left to suspect) and becomes the clean regression test in Phase 5.\\r\\n\\r\\nDone when **every remaining element is load-bearing**: removing any one of them makes the loop go green.\\r\\n\\r\\nDo not proceed until you have reproduced **and** minimised.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Phase 3: Hypothesise\\r\\n\\r\\nGenerate **3–5 ranked hypotheses** before testing any of them. Single-hypothesis generation anchors on the first plausible idea.\\r\\n\\r\\nEach hypothesis must be **falsifiable**: state the prediction it makes.\\r\\n\\r\\n> Format: \\\"If <X> is the cause, then <changing Y> will make the bug disappear / <changing Z> will make it worse.\\\"\\r\\n\\r\\nIf you cannot state the prediction, the hypothesis is a vibe: discard or sharpen it.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Show the ranked list to the user before testing.** They often have domain knowledge that re-ranks instantly (\\\"we just deployed a change to #3\\\"), or know hypotheses they've already ruled out. Cheap checkpoint, big time saver. Don't block on it; proceed with your ranking if the user is AFK.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Phase 4: Instrument\\r\\n\\r\\nEach probe must map to a specific prediction from Phase 3. **Change one variable at a time.**\\r\\n\\r\\nTool preference:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Debugger / REPL inspection** if the env supports it. One breakpoint beats ten logs.\\r\\n2. **Targeted logs** at the boundaries that distinguish hypotheses.\\r\\n3. Never \\\"log everything and grep\\\".\\r\\n\\r\\n**Tag every debug log** with a unique prefix, e.g. `[DEBUG-a4f2]`. Cleanup at the end becomes a single grep. Untagged logs survive; tagged logs die.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Perf branch.** For performance regressions, logs are usually wrong. Instead: establish a baseline measurement (timing harness, `performance.now()`, profiler, query plan), then bisect. Measure first, fix second.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Phase 5: Fix + regression test\\r\\n\\r\\nWrite the regression test **before the fix**, but only if there is a **correct seam** for it.\\r\\n\\r\\nA correct seam is one where the test exercises the **real bug pattern** as it occurs at the call site. If the only available seam is too shallow (single-caller test when the bug needs multiple callers, unit test that can't replicate the chain that triggered the bug), a regression test there gives false confidence.\\r\\n\\r\\n**If no correct seam exists, that itself is the finding.** Note it. The codebase architecture is preventing the bug from being locked down. Flag this for the next phase.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf a correct seam exists:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Turn the minimised repro into a failing test at that seam.\\r\\n2. Watch it fail.\\r\\n3. Apply the fix.\\r\\n4. Watch it pass.\\r\\n5. Skip phases only when explicitly justified.\r\n\r\nWhen exploring the codebase, read `CONTEXT.md` (if it exists) to get a clear mental model of the relevant modules, and check ADRs in the area you're touching.\r\n\r\n## Redact\r\n\r\nThis skill has you show commands, outputs and captured artifacts. **Redact every secret first**: write `<REDACTED>` in its place. If you don't have one, no amount of staring at code will save you.\r\n\r\nSpend disproportionate effort here. **Be aggressive. Be creative. Refuse to give up.**\r\n\r\n### Ways to construct one, in roughly this order\r\n\r\n1. **Failing test** at whatever seam reaches the bug: unit, integration, e2e.\r\n2. **Curl / HTTP script** against a running dev server.\r\n3. **CLI invocation** with a fixture input, diffing stdout against a known-good snapshot.\r\n4. **Headless browser script** (Playwright / Puppeteer) that drives the UI and asserts on DOM/console/network.\r\n5. **Replay a captured trace.** Save a real network request / payload / event log to disk; replay it through the code path in isolation.\r\n6. **Throwaway harness.** Spin up a minimal subset of the system (one service, mocked deps) that exercises the bug code path with a single function call.\r\n7. **Property / fuzz loop.** If the bug is \"sometimes wrong output\", run 1000 random inputs and look for the failure mode.\r\n8. **Bisection harness.** If the bug appeared between two known states (commit, dataset, version), automate \"boot at state X, check, repeat\" so you can `git bisect run` it.\r\n9. **Differential loop.** Run the same input through old-version vs new-version (or two configs) and diff outputs.\r\n10. **HITL bash script.** Last resort. If a human must click, drive _them_ with `scripts/hitl-loop.template.sh` so the loop is still structured. Captured output feeds back to you.\r\n\r\nBuild the right feedback loop, and the bug is 90% fixed.\r\n\r\n### Tighten the loop\r\n\r\nTreat the loop as a product. Once you have _a_ loop, **tighten** it:\r\n\r\n- Can I make it faster? (Cache setup, skip unrelated init, narrow the test scope.)\r\n- Can I make the signal sharper? (Assert on the specific symptom, not \"didn't crash\".)\r\n- Can I make it more deterministic? (Pin time, seed RNG, isolate filesystem, freeze network.)\r\n\r\nA 30-second flaky loop is barely better than no loop; a 2-second deterministic one is tight, a debugging superpower.\r\n\r\n### Non-deterministic bugs\r\n\r\nThe goal is not a clean repro but a **higher reproduction rate**. Loop the trigger 100×, parallelise, add stress, narrow timing windows, inject sleeps. Watch it go red as the bug appears.\r\n\r\nConfirm:\r\n\r\n- [ ] The loop produces the failure mode the **user** described, not a different failure that happens to be nearby. Cut inputs, callers, config, data, and steps **one at a time**, re-running the loop after each cut, and keep only what's load-bearing for the failure.\r\n\r\nWhy bother: a minimal repro shrinks the hypothesis space in Phase 3 (fewer moving parts left to suspect) and becomes the clean regression test in Phase 5.\r\n\r\nDone when **every remaining element is load-bearing**: removing any one of them makes the loop go green.\r\n\r\nDo not proceed until you have reproduced **and** minimised.\r\n\r\n## Phase 3: Hypothesise\r\n\r\nGenerate **3–5 ranked hypotheses** before testing any of them. Single-hypothesis generation anchors on the first plausible idea.\r\n\r\nEach hypothesis must be **falsifiable**: state the prediction it makes.\r\n\r\n> Format: \"If <X> is the cause, then <changing Y> will make the bug disappear / <changing Z> will make it worse.\"\r\n\r\nIf you cannot state the prediction, the hypothesis is a vibe: discard or sharpen it.\r\n\r\n**Show the ranked list to the user before testing.** They often have domain knowledge that re-ranks instantly (\"we just deployed a change to #3\"), or know hypotheses they've already ruled out.
